content: This document provides a summary of information about the product but does not include all possible details. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your use. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice and should not replace the guidance of your healthcare professional. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Side Effects: Common side effects may include stomach upset, headache, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile), which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection (fungal infections in the mouth or vagina). Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before taking cefaclor, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, penicillins, other cephalosporins, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Cefaclor may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. Cefaclor passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., some diabetic urine tests), potentially causing false test results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication in the refrigerator. Do not freeze it. Discard any unused portion after 14 days. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Notes: This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it later for another infection unless directed by your doctor. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete and personalized information about this product and your health needs.
